Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 69, verse 24–32:

﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you put forward﴾ in (the good deeds) you sent ahead for your Hereafter ﴿in the days gone by﴾, meaning the days of the world (dunya).

﴿But as for him who is given his record in his left hand﴾. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: his left hand is twisted [from his chest] [[Addition from manuscript "b".]] behind his back, and then his record is given to him. It is also said: his left hand is pulled from his chest to behind his back, and then his record is given to him. ﴿He will say: "Oh, I wish I had not been given my record, and had not known what my account is!"﴾ He wishes that he had not been given his record, because of the evil deeds he sees in it.

﴿Oh, I wish it had been the end (that decided everything)!﴾ He says: I wish the death I died in the world had been the decisive death, empty of anything after it and cutting off life, so that I would not have lived after it. "Al-qadiya" is a death after which there is no life. He wishes he had not been raised for the reckoning. Qatadah said: he wishes for death, and there was nothing more hateful to him in the world than death.

﴿My wealth has not availed me﴾ it did not ward off from me any of the punishment of Allah.

﴿My authority has perished from me﴾ my proof has gone astray from me, according to most of the exegetes. Ibn Zayd said: my dominion and my power have departed from me. Muqatil said: meaning when his limbs testify against him to his polytheism, Allah says to the guardians of Hell: ﴿Seize him and shackle him﴾, gather his hand to his neck.

﴿Then burn him in the Blazing Fire﴾, that is: cast him into Hell.

﴿Then insert him into a chain, its length seventy cubits, so enter him therein﴾ so make him enter it. Ibn Abbas said: seventy cubits by the cubit of the angel, so it enters his anus and exits from his nostril. It is also said: it enters his mouth and exits from his anus. Nawf al-Bakali said: seventy cubits, each cubit seventy spans, each span further than the distance between you and Makkah, and it was in the courtyard of Kufa. Sufyan said: each cubit is seventy cubits. al-Hasan said: Allah knows best what cubit it is.

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tawbah informed us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith informed us, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i informed us, Abdullah ibn Mahmud informed us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khallal narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Yazid, from Abu al-Samh, from Isa ibn Hilal al-Sadafi, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If a [rudaduda] [[Both manuscripts read "rudaduda," and so does Ibn Kathir. Sharh al-Sunnah reads "rudraduda," while al-Tirmidhi, Imam Ahmad and al-Tabari read "rasasa." Al-Mubarakfuri explained it as a piece of lead.]] like this one, pointing to something like a skull, were sent down from the sky to the earth, and it is a distance of five hundred years, it would reach the earth before nightfall. And if it were sent from the top of the chain, it would travel for forty autumns, night and day, before reaching its base or its bottom."

And from Ka'b, who said: If all the iron of the world were gathered, it would not weigh a single ring of it.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 69, verses 40–45:**

﴿Indeed, it﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿is the word of a noble Messenger﴾, that is, the recitation of a noble Messenger, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe. Nor is it the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember﴾.
